course_name_original: Tratamiento y Reciclaje de Residuos Sólidos y Suelos
course_name_en: Treatment and Recycling of Solid Waste and Soils
prerequisites: Clear concepts of chemistry, in the application of material, energy, and mechanical energy balances.

learning_outcomes.text: Consult and effectively use regulations on waste and contaminated soils, demonstrating knowledge of the most significant requirements.
Correctly prepare and present, both orally and in writing, reports on the identification of waste generated in an activity and possible waste minimization alternatives.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the different technologies for waste recovery, treatment, and disposal, performing the necessary calculations for the design of equipment used in treatment.
Demonstrate knowledge of the methodology to be applied for the evaluation of soil contamination.
Select the most viable option for the management of contaminated soils based on their characteristics and applicable regulations.

syllabus_topics: Waste Management: EU thematic strategy and IPPC regulations in waste management
Urban Waste. Collection and transport systems.
Biological treatment methods: composting and biomethanization
Thermal waste treatment processes: incineration of MSW
Controlled landfilling of MSW: Biogas management and leachate treatment
Construction and demolition waste: recycling and landfilling
Incineration of industrial waste. Hospital waste
Solidification-Stabilization of HW. Hazardous waste landfill (Security D.)
Contaminated soils. Regulations, sampling and characterization.
Contaminated soils: Risk analysis and generic reference values
Special waste: radioactive, livestock, forest, mining waste

Laboratory practices dedicated to experimentation with operations and processes of waste management: anaerobic biological treatment of organic waste, physico-chemical treatment of industrial waste, adsorption of refractory organic matter from urban waste leachates and inertization treatment of hazardous waste, complemented with a visit to the urban and industrial waste management and treatment center of Asturias (COGERSA) and other potential visits to industrial facilities, in addition to the participation of industrial experts or the Administration.

assessment_methods.method: Exercises, assignments, and presentations developed during the course
Active participation in the development of the course

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, the final grade is calculated by combining exams and continuous assessment. Laboratory practices are mandatory and assessed at 20% of the final grade; a practice report and evaluation test are required. Classroom practices and group tutorials require mandatory attendance (or over 80% justified attendance) and active participation. A final written exam, which may include partial tests, accounts for 60% of the grade. To pass the course, laboratory practices must be positively completed, and the grade for each exam must not be less than 40% of its maximum value. For extraordinary calls, the final grade combines laboratory and classroom practices/group tutorials from the academic year with the grade from the extraordinary final exam. Students who do not attend class will be evaluated by a theoretical-practical exam (70%), a course-related assignment (15%), and mandatory laboratory practices (15%), with the exam needing to be passed to approve the subject. If the exam cut-off grade is not met, the numeric grade obtained in the exam will be recorded as the final grade.
